candidate.name: Mannarasala Sree Nagaraja Temple
candidate.reason: One of Kerala’s most important serpent-grove shrines — a vast living kaavu with thousands of serpent idols, distinctive women‑centred priestly traditions and fertility rites that make it a unique cultural and visitor experience.

warnings: 2 contact(s) dropped: source page not retrieved or details malformed

claims.claim: Mannarasala Sree Nagaraja Temple address: Mannarasala P.O., Haripad, Alappuzha, PIN 690514.
Published darshan timings (general schedule): Mon–Sat 05:00–11:00 and 05:30–07:30; Sunday 05:00–12:00 and 05:30–07:30.
Temple Office phones: 0479 2413214 and 0479 2410200; guest house phones given on the official site.
The temple grove is commonly described as covering about 16 acres.

Published accounts differ: some modern guides say ~30,000 serpent images, several government/tourism and press sources state over 100,000; the official temple site does not publish a single definitive count.
The temple’s chief priest (the Mannarasala Amma) is a woman from the Mannarasala Illam; the Amma observes a life of austerity while performing her duties and the office is hereditary in the family.
Sarpam Pattu is rare and is scheduled roughly once every 41 years; the temple page records observances in named Malayalam Era years and gives the 1151 M.E. (1976 C.E.) entry.
Photography and videography are strictly prohibited within the temple compound except where the temple gives prior written permission.
Many commonly performed offerings and their rates (the temple lists 51 offerings) can be booked online; the offerings page publishes sample rates and timings.
The nearest railway station is Haripad (station code HAD); the temple information lists Haripad as the nearest rail point at about 2 km.
Nearest airports and approximate road distances published by the temple: Cochin (COK) ≈ 114–120 km; Trivandrum (TRV) ≈ 140 km.
During Ayilyam festival days (Kanni, Thulam, Kumbham) the idols in the grove are carried to the Illam in a procession (Ezhunnallathu) and the Illam hosts special Aayilyam rites.
The temple warns that entry into protected grove areas is forbidden and asks visitors to use designated paths and to avoid touching idols or ritual items.
The temple’s address and guest‑house contact details are published on the official site and the temple operates an Annadanam (free food) and payasam/appam counters during darshan hours.
